# The directory: who People lists, what a search finds, and where old addresses lead

People’s order and search, a page at a time; the line beside a person; a team’s people and goals by status; and where People’s and Teams’ old Workspace addresses now lead.

## The rule

**Who is listed.** Everyone in the workspace except people marked as left (or deleted), by name A to Z, ignoring case and accents; two people with one name are ordered by email, then ID. 50 at a time; a page past the end is the last page.

**What a search finds.** A person matches when every word typed starts a word of their name, their job title or their team’s name, ignoring case and accents (so “eng man” finds “Engineering Manager”, and “lucia” finds “Lucía”). Words are split at spaces and at the punctuation inside names (“Build & Release”, “Cloud Cost (FinOps)”). A team filter keeps the team’s people as `teamPeople` gives them: its lead counts, wherever their own team is; “no team” keeps people with no team or a team that is gone. Teams match on the team’s name or its lead’s, and are listed A to Z.

**A person’s line**, beside them in a list: “Admin”; then “leads the team” (their own), “leads {team}” (another, the first A to Z) or “leads {n} teams”; then their goals in the running cycle that aren’t stopped (“{n} goals”, “1 goal”, “no goals”). The first part takes a capital.

**A team’s summary**: its lead, its people (its lead among them) and its goals in the running cycle counted by status, worst first, from the same statuses Goals uses, so a team’s counts on People and under Goals’ By team are the same numbers.

**Old addresses.** /workspace/people leads to /people, keeping its query; with ?team=<id> it leads to that team’s page; /workspace/teams leads to /teams; /workspace#people and #teams to People and Teams. Each is a replace, not a new history entry.

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| The demo workspace on Wednesday 11 November: People with nothing asked. | `97 people; 1 to 50 of page 1 of 2; first Adaeze Obi` |
| The same, page 9. | `page 2: 51 to 97` |
| Searching for “rhea”, “lucia” and “Romero”. | `Rhea Kapoor / Lucía Romero / Lucía Romero` |
| The CI/CD team’s people, and the admins. | `7 people / Amara Nwosu, Grace Achterberg, Hamid Rezaei` |
| Teams whose name or lead starts with “rhea”. | `CI/CD` |
| The lines beside Amara, Rhea and Oskar. | `Admin · leads the team · no goals / Leads the team · 8 goals / No goals` |
| CI/CD’s summary. | `led by Rhea Kapoor; 7 people; 17 goals` |
| Old addresses: /workspace/people?team=cicd, /workspace/people?team=-, /workspace/teams, /workspace#people. | `/teams/cicd, /people?team=-, /teams, /people` |

## Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** The page size (50) and the reading of “a word” (split at spaces and at & / ( ) , . -) are choices; a rebuild with a server search should keep the rule that every word typed starts a word.
- **Not self-explanatory:** Who leads a team is not a role: a lead is any person a team names, in any team.

## Where it lives

- [src/domain/directory.ts](../../../src/domain/directory.ts): `findInDirectory`, `matchesWords`, `byName`, `findTeams`, `personLine`, `teamSummary`, `movedTo`, `DIRECTORY_PAGE`

## Requirements

- `PEOPLE-DIRECTORY`: Anyone finds a person or a team, and gets from either to their goals (app redesign WR1). People (/people, in the sidebar; on a phone under More) lists everyone not marked as left, A to Z ignoring case and accents, 50 a page; a search matches when every word typed starts a word of the name, job title or team; filters for a team (its lead counts) or no team, and admins only; everything in the address. A row links to the person, with their job title, team and line (Admin; what they lead; their goals this year). A person's page: team, email, role here, goals counted by status as shape and word (each a link to those goals), reviews, and "See {name}’s goals". Teams (/teams) lists each team with its lead, people and goals by status, the same numbers as Goals' By team; a team's page says what it is here to do, its goals by status and its people, with "See its goals". Members see no control that changes anything; admins add, change and mark people as left, and add, change and remove teams there.
- `OLD-ADDRESSES`: Every address that worked before still lands on the right page, without a history entry and keeping its query: /workspace/people goes to /people, /workspace/people?team=<id> to that team's page, /workspace/teams to /teams, and /workspace#people and #teams to People and Teams (domain/directory movedTo).

### [src/domain/directory.test.ts](../../../src/domain/directory.test.ts)

- the directory’s order and search (rule 4) › lists everyone, A to Z, 50 a page
- the directory’s order and search (rule 4) › turns pages, and a page past the end is the last page
- the directory’s order and search (rule 4) › finds by the start of a word of the name, ignoring case and accents
- the directory’s order and search (rule 4) › finds by job title, every word typed starting a word
- the directory’s order and search (rule 4) › finds a team’s people by the team’s name, and anyone with it in their job title, once each
- the directory’s order and search (rule 4) › filters by team (its lead counts), by no team, and by admins
- the directory’s order and search (rule 4) › never lists anyone marked as left
- the directory’s order and search (rule 4) › keeps two people with one name in a stable order, by email
- the directory’s order and search (rule 4) › matches words, not the middle of one
- teams (rule 4) › lists the teams A to Z, found by name or by lead
- a person’s line and a team’s summary (rule 5) › says admin, what they lead and how many goals
- a person’s line and a team’s summary (rule 5) › says which other team someone leads, or how many
- a person’s line and a team’s summary (rule 5) › counts a team’s people, its lead among them, and its goals by status as Goals’ By team does
- a person’s line and a team’s summary (rule 5) › a team with no goals has no counts; a lead from another team is one of its people
- old addresses (rule 8) › %s%s%s leads to %s
